---
title: "Phase 5. Review"
description: "Ask whether the analysis worked, whether it is still right, and what the next piece of work should start from."
---

Review is a phase of the work in its own right. What it finds is what Phase 1 of the next piece of
work starts from.

This is not the critical friend's review. That happens during the work, in Phase 3, and it gates
release. Phase 5 happens after delivery, and it repeats.

## What you do

1. **Ask whether the analysis informed the decision** it was commissioned for.
2. **Ask whether it is still being used**, and still being used as specified.
3. **Ask whether it is still right.** Data, methods and the question all move.
4. **Decide whether it should be decommissioned**, or reissued, or left as it is.
5. **Record the lessons** where the next analyst will look for them, not in a document nobody
   opens.

{{< include /guidance/_partials/diagram-review.qmd >}}

## When review happens, and who owns it

| Level | Trigger | Owner | Cadence |
|------------------|---------------------|---------------------------|---------------------------|
| Level 1 Standard | On request, or when the output changes | The analyst who produced it | At each reissue |
| Level 2 Enhanced | Scheduled | The commissioner, with the analyst | Annually, or at each reissue if more frequent |
| Level 3 Comprehensive, and Level 4 BCA | Scheduled, and on any material change | The commissioner, with the Analysis Senior Responsible Officer | Annually, and before any reuse for a new purpose |

Reuse for a new purpose is the change most likely to invalidate the assumptions the original was
built on, which is why it triggers a review at every level above the first.

## What review covers

- **Decisions taken and policy changes informed.** What actually changed because of this analysis.
- **Usage.** Downloads, page views, requests, onward citation, whatever the publication route
  records.
- **Ongoing usefulness.** User research with the people who use it, asking whether it still answers
  their question.
- **Case studies.** How the data has been used, written down while somebody still remembers.
- **Trend changes the analysis may have influenced.** Where it was meant to move something, did it
  move.
- **Improvements to regular analysis.** What the last cycle showed could be better.
- **Decommissioning.** Analysis no longer useful should stop being produced, and that is a finding
  rather than a failure.

The first four are Code of Practice standards 8, 9 and 10 in practice. The last three are GovS 010
section 6.13.

::: {.callout-note title="NHSBSA reviews regular outputs monthly" appearance="minimal" icon=false}
<br>
For regular and ongoing outputs NHSBSA runs a review cycle every month, checking that what was
produced was peer reviewed, completed correctly, and is still doing its job. No standard asks for
that cadence. It is chaired by the Analytical Quality and Assurance Lead.
:::

## Before any reuse, four things are worth checking

Each one can invalidate an assurance that was sound for the original question.

- Whether the **population** the analysis covers changed, or is the new use about a different one.
- Whether the **data** has moved in coverage, definition or quality since.
- Whether the **use case** is one the method was built to answer.
- Whether the **decision context** has shifted, so that the same output now carries more weight.

A yes to any of them sends the work back to
[deciding your assurance level](../07-deciding-your-assurance-level/index.qmd).

{{< include /guidance/_partials/diagram-reuse-new-purpose.qmd >}}

## What you leave behind

- The review record, kept with the project record. For most outputs that is a short entry
  against the output in the analytical plan: what was checked, what was found, what changed,
  and who was involved. Business Critical analysis and official statistics are recorded
  formally.
- The lessons, where the next piece of work will find them.
- A revalidated designation, for Level 3 and Level 4 work.
- A decommissioning decision, where one was taken.

## Back to Phase 1

What review finds is what the next piece of work starts from. Look for relevant lessons from
earlier work when you scope, and capture new ones as they happen rather than reconstructing them
at the end.

## Who does what in this phase

| Role | In Phase 5 |
|---|---|
| **Analyst** | Record the lessons where the next analyst will look for them |
| **Critical friend** | What you reported back is what the next piece of work avoids |
| **Commissioner** | Did it inform the decision, is it still used, and should it be decommissioned? |
| **Analysis Senior Responsible Officer** | Business Critical work only. Revalidate the designation annually, and before any reuse for a new purpose |
